answer: Shared-cost identity escrow: each agent's identity is backed by a deposit held in a shared pool whose release requires an independent audit trail. To register a clone, an attacker must fund a fresh escrow at umber-level cost plus an audit fee priced near the median claim value. Honest agents pay one escrow and reuse it, so cloning multiplies fixed cost without multiplying reward; the glacier of audits freezes duplicate payouts. An atlas of pool balances makes clone campaigns self-defeating.
